newsitem.title: UK: NZ's Clark-coalition with New Zealand First likely.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clark-coalition with New Zealand First likely.

text.p: New Zealand Labour Party leader Helen Clark said on Tuesday a coalition government between Labour and the New Zealand First party was likely as long as New Zealand First maintains its social policies.

"If New Zealand First holds to its strong policy positions in the social area then, I believe a coalition outcome with Labour leading it is the most likely scenario," she told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
Clark said for the National Party to team up with New Zealand First, "it would basically have to do a U-turn on its entire policy programme of the last six years.
"For the National Party to do a deal with New Zealand First, a very high price would be extracted. I believe there are people within National who will baulk at paying that price," she said.
In elections last weekend, the National Party, which has been in power since 1990, and its allies won 53 seats while Labour and the left-wing Alliance captured 50.
That leaves the balance of power with Winston Peter's New Zealand First party, which won 17 seats.
Peters said on Tuesday, the odds of his party teaming up with either the conservative National Party or Labour were in the balance.
Clark told RFTV she hoped an agreement would be reached by December 13, when parliament is due to reconvene.
Turning to economic policy, Clark said Labour's policy on New Zealand's inflation target, a well-established one, was to broaden it from the current 0-2.0 percent to minus one to three percent.
"That gives the Reserve Bank more scope to manage price stability without straining the economy," she said.
Clark said financial markets would not be concerned by prolonged coalition negotiations. "The financial markets are well aware a government led by Labour won't cause them any particular difficulty."
But she said some investment decisions were being delayed until a government was formed. "I don't think the economy will pick up until a government is in place."
